coverage.r2: Speaking Arabic only 06:26-10:31 (date, weather, clothes) plus 38:13, 41:10, 44:46, 1:00:47; 11:07-1:00:35 is a listening/translation drill on make-X/get-X verbs, written as mode=listening. Engine noise: 47:22 'too much fucked' (her زعجتو), 49:06 'My choose Aloo' (ما تزعلوا), 18:43 'Ma bistah'. No echo-candidates file for 2026-09-19.

r3_note: Almost all of this lesson (11:13-1:00:35) is a listening drill on make-X / get-X verbs: Medi translates Amal's Arabic, so most rows are mode=listening. Ending/prefix misreads were ruled grammar (B1/B5/B10/B12/B18/D3/D4); only a different root (زعل vs زعج) stays vocab.

rows.medi_said: This is it today. تسعة عشرين.
rows.why: He said 29 for the date 19 (a different number = different word, tier 1); Amal said '19' and he took it at 06:42 تسعة عشر.
rows.r3_why: Real slip; tier 1 (wrong number, not a wrong form of the right one), Amal's bare '19' is a recast he took.

rows.medi_said: I said, uh, ستة عشر ستة
rows.why: He gave the month as 6; Amal questioned ستة؟ and gave تسعطاش تسعة (19/9), chat 'tese3ta3sh tes3a'.

rows.medi_said: اليوم الجو بتغي-- بتغير كتير.
rows.amal_said: So تغير، no be. ... It changed؟
rows.chat: el-jaw el-yoam t8ayyar kteer u shob mish m8ayyem
rows.why: He used the present b- form for something that already happened; Amal: 'So تغير, no be', he: 'past tense, you're right'.
rows.english: The weather today changed a lot.

rows.medi_said: أب المامبارح or أب الامبارح? أب الامبارح.
rows.amal_said: قبل امبارح or أول امبارح some people say.
rows.why: He put el- on امبارح ('2abel el-mbare7'); Amal answered with قبل امبارح / أول امبارح without el-; he still repeated أب الامبارح at 09:04.

rows.medi_said: أبيض. أبيض. ... بلوز أبيض
rows.why: بلوزة is feminine so the colour must be بيضا; Amal said بيضة (=بيضا) right after his أبيض; he then switched to قميص (chat 2amees rasmi abyad).

rows.medi_said: uh، كمي
rows.why: He stalled after أزرق on a word the engine wrote كمي (maybe كحلي 'navy'); Amal supplied غامق and he repeated it - she gave the word he lacked, so tier 0.
rows.r3_why: Real help from Amal mid-sentence, but كمي is not a clear wrong word (could be كحلي, a right word); tier 0 = she supplied it, low confidence.

rows.medi_said: you are tired of me.
rows.why: Misread تعبتني as 'tired of me'; Amal: 'No that's تعبت مني'.
rows.r3_challenge: Wrong label: 'you are tired of me' for تعبتني is the make-X vs get-X misreading (Amal: 'that's تعبت مني. تعبتني'), same as D6/D11 - grammar B12, not vocab tier 1.

rows.medi_said: Why did you smile to a male or why did she smile?
rows.right: why do you laugh / smile (بتضحك present)
rows.why: He read the b- present بتضحك as past; Amal 'Is it did or do?' and he fixed at 15:58 'Why do you smile? Present tense'.
rows.r3_why: The fix is the b- = present rule (B1), so grammar, not vocab.

rows.medi_said: Isn't this to inflict sadness? The past tense. ... Okay, I was sad.
rows.amal_said: That's زهقت. زهقت. ... زهقت مش زعلت.
rows.why: Read زهقت as زعلت (sad); Amal 'زهقت مش زعلت'.

rows.medi_said: They had fun or they enjoyed?
rows.amal_said: آآآ. Close بس that would be انبسطوا. انبسطوا
rows.why: Her chat enbes6u is the command form (vs past enbasa6u she types at 1:02:22); he read it as 'they had fun', Amal 'Close but that would be enbasa6u'; he moved to 'you guys' but never to a command.
rows.r3_why: Real slip (Amal 'Close but'); the chat spelling enbes6u vs enbasa6u shows command vs past, so B10 rather than B5.

rows.medi_said: What boring hap-- What happened boring?
rows.why: Took بيزعل as بيزهق; Amal 'No, بيزعل مش بيزهق'.

rows.medi_said: He will not, he will not bore you.
rows.amal_said: Very close. أزهقك، not يزهقك. أزهقك.
rows.why: He read the I-prefix of أزهقك as the he-prefix; Amal 'أزهقك not يزهقك', 'I won't bore you'.
rows.r3_why: Real; the slip is the person prefix on the verb (B18), not a different word, so grammar.

rows.medi_said: Were you sad from what happened?
rows.amal_said: Very close. بس مش sad. انزعجتي.
rows.why: Read انزعجتي as sad; Amal 'مش sad'.
rows.english: Did you get annoyed at what happened?

rows.medi_said: so don't be tired of me.
rows.amal_said: That's ما تتعبي مني. ما تعبيني.
rows.why: He read the make-X form تعبيني as get-X; Amal contrasted ما تتعبي مني vs ما تعبيني and he fixed to 'don't make me tired'.
rows.r3_why: make-X vs get-X is B12 grammar.

rows.medi_said: She laughed at him.
rows.why: He read the ending on علي as عليه; Amal repeated علي, he fixed 'She laughed at me', she then said 'علي and عليه'.
rows.r3_why: Person ending on a preposition = D3.

rows.medi_said: Who was he mad with you-- at you? I don't... This doesn't make sense.
rows.amal_said: What's ضايقك؟ ... So is it ضايق or it's ضايقة to be upset؟
rows.wrong: who was he mad at you
rows.why: He could not read make-X ضايقك (took it as 'be mad'); Amal prompted 'What's ضايقك? ... ضايق or تضايق to be upset?' until he said 'who made you upset' at 28:17.
rows.r3_why: Real; her prompts are about make-X vs get-X (ضايق vs تضايق), so B12 grammar rather than vocab.

rows.medi_said: So basat is I was happy.
rows.why: He read make-X بسطه as get-X 'I was happy' (after 'So I am happy... No' at 32:21); Amal 'So بسطت first. I made.' and he fixed at 32:46 'I made him happy'.

rows.medi_said: Matahammasi... Uh, Lisa ma-- Or matahammasi Lisa.
rows.why: He dropped the you-form te- of the t- verb (ma ta7ammasi); Amal recast ما تتحمسي لسه and he said 'Oh, that's right'.
rows.r3_challenge: Wrong bucket: his ma is right (B11 is ma vs la); the slip is the missing t- of the tet- prefix (matahammasi for ma tet7ammasi) - a form slip, possibly only S4 sound; audio check.

rows.medi_said: Yeah, they apologized. Present tense.
rows.why: He called past اتأسفوا present; Amal 'لأ, اتأسفوا not بيتأسفوا' and he fixed.
rows.r3_why: Past vs present recognition = B5 grammar.

rows.medi_said: Oh, khirbat. Uh, she ruined the trip.
rows.amal_said: No؟ ... That would be خربت. خربت.
rows.why: He read get-X خِربت (got ruined) as make-X 'ruined'; first 'I ruined' at 39:31 (Amal 'Are you sure? I ruined?'), then 'she ruined' - 'No? That would be خرّبت'; he fixed at 40:14 'the trip was ruined'.
rows.r3_why: make-X vs get-X = B12; one row for the 39:31-39:47 run.

rows.medi_said: who was made happy or who enjoyed from us?
rows.why: Heard معنا as منا; Amal 'With us. معنا.', he said 'I was saying mina'.

rows.medi_said: Uh, are you excited to a girl?
rows.why: He read past تحمستِ as present 'are you excited'; Amal recast 'Did you get excited?' and he repeated it at 43:25.
rows.r3_why: Her English recast is a voiced fix of the tense he gave; he took it.

rows.medi_said: bizah.
rows.amal_said: Yeah. That's boring. ... زهقان. ... It's بس زهق، زهق.
rows.why: Asked for 'bored' he gave بيزهق (boring / it bores); Amal said 'That's boring' and supplied زهقان.

rows.medi_said: uh, you guys don't, don't be annoyed.
rows.why: He read زعل (sad) as annoyed (زعج, another root); Amal 'Annoyed?' and he fixed at 49:38 'don't be sad'.
rows.r3_why: Different lexical item (زعل vs زعج) = vocab tier 1.

rows.medi_said: She was happy. ... I enjoyed to it.
rows.amal_said: No، انبسطت له. ... Just the verb. I got happy له. ... For، for him.
rows.right: I got happy for him (انبسطت له)
rows.why: Her 'No' answers 'I enjoyed to it': he misread له; she said 'For, for him' and he fixed at 50:53 'I got happy for him'. 'She was happy' alone was not wrong (her chat gives enbasa6etlo too).
rows.r3_why: Real slip on the ending of the preposition له (D3); the person was not the error.

rows.medi_said: You guys don't be annoyed.
rows.why: He read make-X تزعجوه as get-X تنزعجوا; Amal named both forms; he reached 'don't be annoying to him' at 53:17.

rows.medi_said: They made us sad.
rows.why: He read the object ending -ني as 'us'; Amal repeated زعلوني and he fixed 'They made me sad'.
rows.r3_why: Object ending on a verb = D4.

rows.medi_said: So it made me happy...
rows.amal_said: صح، it made happy، بس is it past or present؟
rows.why: He read b- present بيبسطني as past; Amal 'past or present?', he fixed 'it makes me happy'.
rows.english: It makes me happy to come.

rows.medi_said: Did, uh, did you guys enjoy to me? ... I don't understand this one.
rows.amal_said: Great that you got the [لي] part صح. They got-- they were happy for me.
rows.why: Amal praised the لي part (engine wrote 'day part') and fixed the person: -u = they, not you guys (-tu); chat enbasa6uli; he took 'They were happy for me'.
rows.r3_why: Her fix is the past-tense person ending (B5), not the preposition, which she said he got right.
